# Exact normalized values independently preserve matches despite changes or missing values in other attributes.
def exact_normalized(r):
    import re
    import unicodedata
    import hashlib

    def norm(value):
        value = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value or "").casefold()
        value = "".join(
            c for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", value)
            if unicodedata.category(c) != "Mn"
        )
        return " ".join(re.findall(r"\w+", value, flags=re.UNICODE))

    def key(prefix, value):
        digest = hashlib.blake2b(value.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=10).hexdigest()
        return prefix + digest

    out = []
    title = norm(r.get("title", ""))
    brand = norm(r.get("brand", ""))
    description = norm(r.get("description", ""))
    price = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", r.get("price", "") or "").casefold()
    amounts = re.findall(r"\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?", price)

    if title:
        out.append(key("xt:", title))
    if brand:
        out.append(key("xb:", brand))
    if len(description) >= 8:
        out.append(key("xd:", description))
    for amount in amounts[:2]:
        amount = amount.replace(",", ".").lstrip("0") or "0"
        out.append("xp:" + amount)
    return list(dict.fromkeys(out))


# Structural identifiers and long lexical anchors tolerate reordered text, compound separators, and surrounding boilerplate.
def token_anchors(r):
    import re
    import unicodedata

    def norm(value):
        value = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value or "").casefold()
        value = "".join(
            c for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", value)
            if unicodedata.category(c) != "Mn"
        )
        value = re.sub(r"(?<=[a-z])(?=\d)|(?<=\d)(?=[a-z])", " ", value)
        return re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", value, flags=re.UNICODE)

    text = " ".join([
        r.get("title", ""),
        r.get("brand", ""),
        r.get("description", ""),
    ])
    tokens = norm(text)
    candidates = set()

    for token in tokens:
        compact = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", token)
        has_alpha = bool(re.search(r"[a-z]", compact))
        has_digit = bool(re.search(r"\d", compact))
        if len(compact) >= 4 and has_alpha and has_digit:
            candidates.add(("id:", compact, 100 + len(compact)))
        elif len(token) >= 6:
            rarity = sum(c in "qzxjvkwy" for c in token)
            candidates.add(("tk:", token, len(token) + 3 * rarity))

    ranked = sorted(candidates, key=lambda x: (-x[2], x[1]))
    return [prefix + value[:40] for prefix, value, _ in ranked[:8]]


# Seeded character-shingle minima provide fuzzy title signatures for insertions, deletions, spelling noise, and reordered wording.
def character_minhash(r):
    import re
    import unicodedata
    import hashlib

    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", r.get("title", "") or "").casefold()
    text = "".join(
        c for c in unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
        if unicodedata.category(c) != "Mn"
    )
    text = re.sub(r"[^\w]+", "", text, flags=re.UNICODE)
    if not text:
        return []

    width = 3 if len(text) < 80 else 4
    shingles = {text[i:i + width] for i in range(max(1, len(text) - width + 1))}
    if len(text) < width:
        shingles = {text}

    out = []
    for seed in range(5):
        best = min(
            hashlib.blake2b(
                (str(seed) + "|" + shingle).encode("utf-8"),
                digest_size=8
            ).hexdigest()
            for shingle in shingles
        )
        out.append("mh%d:" % seed + best)
    return out


# Rare-character presence is a coarse multilingual fallback for heavily rewritten records with little stable metadata.
def rare_character_fallback(r):
    import unicodedata

    text = " ".join([
        r.get("title", ""),
        r.get("brand", ""),
        r.get("price", ""),
        r.get("description", ""),
    ])
    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text).casefold()
    text = "".join(c for c in text if unicodedata.category(c) != "Mn")

    rare = "qzxjvkwy"
    out = ["rc:" + c for c in rare if c in text]
    scripts = set()
    for c in text:
        if not c.isalpha() or c.isascii():
            continue
        name = unicodedata.name(c, "")
        if name:
            scripts.add(name.split()[0])
    out.extend("us:" + script[:12].lower() for script in sorted(scripts)[:2])
    return out


SCHEMES = {
    "exact_normalized": exact_normalized,
    "token_anchors": token_anchors,
    "character_minhash": character_minhash,
    "rare_character_fallback": rare_character_fallback,
}
